chunks: And Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said:

A man died during the time of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام and left behind a son and a slave. Each one of them claimed that he was the son and that the other was his slave. So they came to Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام and sought judgment from him. Then Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام ordered that two holes be made in the wall of the mosque. Then he ordered each one of them to put his head into a hole, and they did so. Then he said, “O Qanbar, unsheathe the sword,” and he secretly told him, “Do not do what I command you to do.” Then he said, “Strike the neck of the slave.” He said: the slave drew back his head, so Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام seized him and said to the other, “You are the son, and I have freed this one and made him a mawlā for you.”

key_terms.أَعْتَقْتُ: I have freed; declaration of manumission by the Imam عليه السلام
key_terms.أَمِيرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful, referring here to Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام in his governing and judicial role
key_terms.ابْنًا: a son; the rightful heir being identified
key_terms.السَّيْفَ: the sword; used in the Imam’s test to reveal the truth
key_terms.الْمَسْجِدِ: the mosque; the place where the procedure was carried out
key_terms.عَبْدًا: a slave; the disputed legal status in the case
key_terms.فَتَحَاكَمَا: they sought judgment; they brought the dispute for adjudication
key_terms.مَوْلًى: a freed servant or client; the post-manumission relation established here

ai.seo_question: How did Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام judge a case in which a son and a slave each claimed to be the heir?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates a judicial case judged by Amīr al-Muʾminīn Imam ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib عليه السلام, in which two men disputed whether each was the deceased man’s son or slave. By a practical legal stratagem, the Imam عليه السلام exposed the true slave and then freed him, demonstrating discernment in judgment and authority in resolving disputed status.
